title: Mariner Systems - activation intake & networking sync
summary: Kickoff for Mariner Systems activation: discussed onboarding scope, VPC/networking options, security needs (SOC2/KMS/SAML), pilot success metrics, and next steps around pricing and pilot schedule. SE to run a lightweight connectivity test and benchmark plan. Action items assigned for security docs and network diagram.
topics: Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
action_items: Alex - send tailored pricing and committed throughput options by 2026-10-02
Diego - share connectivity test script and sample benchmark dataset by 2026-10-06
Priya - add Mariner to onboarding runbook and schedule kickoff workshop week of 2026-10-12
Linda - provide network diagram and firewall rules by 2026-10-01
next_steps: Schedule technical kickoff workshop (SE + DevOps) — target week of 2026-10-12
Redwood to provide SOC2 cert and security pack link
Start connectivity tests and one-day latency/throughput benchmark on hosted and dedicated variants
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-29 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Evan Park (Mariner CTO), Linda Zhao (Mariner DevOps), Samir Patel (Mariner PM)

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this pretty focused. I'm Alex from Redwood, Priya and Diego are with me. Quick round of intros?
00:09 Evan: Evan, CTO at Mariner Systems. We're building the recommendation and search stack on top of a mix of open models and a few tuned ones, we want to evaluate Redwood for production inference and integration with our VPCs.
00:20 Linda: Linda, I run DevOps. I'll own the network and security side.
00:24 Samir: Samir, product — focused on latency targets and rollout cadence.
00:30 Priya: Great, thanks. Goal for today: align on onboarding scope, network connectivity options, security questions, and pilot success criteria.
00:39 Alex: High level Mariner ask we heard from the form: 99th p95-ish latency sub-350ms for chat rerank flows and sustained qps of ~80-100 across peak windows. Is that still accurate?
00:51 Samir: Yes that's what we care about. Also want predictable cost per request — we have to compare hosted pricing vs dedicated commits.
01:01 Diego: Quick clarifying Q: are you wanting Redwood hosted initially or private/VPC right away?
01:06 Evan: Prefer hosted to start but security wants VPC peering options on day 30. We may move to dedicated reserved capacity if cost and latency line up.
01:17 Priya: Noted. We'll propose a pilot that starts hosted, with a documented migration path to Dedicated and Private.
01:26 Linda: From networking, we need to validate egress IPs, SAML metadata, and ensure KMS integration for any customer-side keys if we go private. Also audit logs retention — 1 year required.
01:39 Diego: We support SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and customers can bring KMS keys for Private deployments; hosted keeps logs in our control but we can provide long-term exports. Small caveat — hosted KMS integration requires dedicated mode for key isolation, I'll note that.
01:57 Linda: Okay, that aligns. Can you share the SOC 2 report and a security pack?
02:03 Alex: Yes — we'll send SOC2 Type II and a security pack link after the call.
02:09 Evan: Timeline question: legal / procurement wants a 60-day pilot window before any commit. Can we accommodate that?
02:15 Priya: That's typical. We propose a 4–8 week pilot with checkpoints at week 2 and week 6, and an internal evaluation rubric.
02:24 Samir: Pilot success metrics: p95 latency < 350ms for the rerank path, inference cost per thousand tokens below our threshold, and functional parity with our test prompts. We'll share a benchmark prompt set.
02:36 Diego: Perfect — we'll use your prompt set and also suggest a small synthetic dataset to measure tail latency under continuous batching.
02:44 Alex: On the cost front, important tradeoffs: batching and caching reduce unit cost but increase tail latency. There is also quantized model variants that cut GPU cost. We can show a cost/latency matrix in the follow-up deck.
02:58 Evan: Sounds good. On the networking approach: we prefer VPC peering but are open to private link / transit gateway if easier. Any constraints on ports or protocols?
03:10 Linda: Our infra team only allows TLS 1.2+, strict egress via proxy, and no inbound from public subnets. We will likely do VPC peering or private-link style setup.
03:21 Diego: We can do VPC peering to our dedicated nodes or configure an endpoint for Private deployment. For hosted there are egress IP ranges and a NAT-based approach. We'll send exact IPs and firewall rules.
03:33 Linda: Great. Also need to understand network footprint for KV cache and streaming — do you use persistent TCP connections for long-lived sessions?
03:43 Diego: We maintain persistent connections for streaming inference when using SDKs — for HTTP REST it's keep-alive. KV cache isn't an extra network call — it's colocated in the runtime, however when you're using a private backend you'll see traffic between your VPC and the nodes for the model serving. Sometimes the transcriber (note: transcription typo: 'transcriber' instead of 'kv').. sorry — the transcript jumped — we meant there are occasional heartbeats.
04:02 (crosstalk) Samir: okay noted.
04:06 Alex: Questions from Mariner's side about encryption and key management?
04:09 Linda: We need to ensure customer-managed keys are possible, and that at-rest encryption uses our keys for private deployments. Also retention of request logs — are those redacted automatically?
04:19 Diego: For Private, yes you can bring your KMS keys and logs live in your S3 bucket optionally. Hosted has configurable log export and PII redaction settings — we'll provide the exact fields that are redacted by default.
04:34 Evan: Any compliance certifications beyond SOC2? ISO? EU data residency?
04:37 Alex: We have SOC2 and pursuing ISO certification — EU region support is available in selected regions for customers requiring residency. We'll include a regional map.
04:47 Linda: Good. Procurement will need an indemnity clause and SLAs — what uptime do you guarantee for Dedicated?
04:53 Priya: Dedicated comes with SLA options — we can provide 99.9% and a more enterprise SLA. We'll include that in the pricing doc.
05:01 Evan: Regarding cost modeling, can you show the breakpoint where Dedicated becomes cheaper than hosted given our qps and token profile?
05:07 Alex: Yes that's a common ask — we'll prepare a cost model for your qps distribution and token lengths. Diego will run a sample benchmark to validate assumptions.
05:16 Diego: I'll need a small dataset and a typical request distribution — if you can share the prompt set and a token histogram, I'll run two runs: hosted cold-run and hosted warmed with caching; and a dedicated run with quantized variant. Expect initial numbers in 4–5 business days post-data.
05:32 Samir: We'll share the prompts and a sample of request sizes by EOD tomorrow.
05:36 (short pause)
05:40 Priya: Operationally, our onboarding playbook has these steps: intake -> network connectivity -> workshop with SE -> pilot run -> evaluation -> rollout. We'll run a 90-day runway doc but compress to meet your procurement 60-day pilot ask.
05:56 Linda: On the connectivity test: what exactly will you test?
05:59 Diego: Basic TCP handshake, TLS verification, latency sampling to edge nodes, and a simple inference end-to-end call with your prompts. I'll provide a script that runs from your bastion.
06:10 Linda: Good — provide the script and we'll schedule the run during a low-traffic window.
06:16 Alex: On the security docs: we'll upload SOC2 Type II, pen test summary, and a security pack link. Also share the SAML metadata for SSO setup.
06:26 Evan: Legal will also want encryption-in-transit details and data retention policy.
06:30 Alex: We'll include those.
06:33 (brief background noise)
06:36 Samir: One other thing — model versioning and rollback. We need to be able to pin models and do canary deploys.
06:42 Diego: Full support for model pinning, canaries, and automated fallback. In Dedicated you can pin a version and set rollout percentages. We'll surface traces per-route in the console.
06:52 Samir: Do you keep token-level cost breakdowns per route?
06:55 Priya: Yes, console has per-route breakdowns and per-token cost estimates. We can export CSVs for internal chargeback.
07:03 Evan: Great. For the pilot we'll aim to run two scenarios: 1) search + rerank path under normal load, 2) peak burst test to evaluate tail latency.
07:14 Diego: Understood. For burst tests we recommend warm caches and a stepped load generator to catch any tail effects.
07:20 (inaudible 07:21-07:23)
07:23 Alex: Anything else we should call out now?
07:26 Linda: Firewall requirements from your side — send egress IP ranges and we'll validate. Also confirm whether private deployments require HSM for key storage.
07:37 Diego: Private can support HSM integrations; I'll note that in the security doc. Egress IPs will be in the network packet we'll send.
07:45 Evan: Who will be our main point of contact for the technical kickoff?
07:49 Priya: Diego will own the SE-side, and I'll coordinate schedules and onboarding tasks. Alex is AE for procurement.
07:57 Alex: Ok recap: Diego shares connectivity script and benchmark plan; Alex sends pricing and SOC2/security pack; Linda shares network diagram and firewall rules; Priya schedules the workshop for week of Oct 12.
08:11 Samir: That covers it. We appreciate the structured plan.
08:15 Alex: We'll follow up with calendar invites and links.
08:18 Evan: Thanks all.

(End of transcript — timestamps are approximate; transcription may contain minor mis-hearings such as 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache' and occasional speaker label noise.)
